meta.title: Unisphere foundation: independent SDK, CLI and proof lanes

architecture.principles: Hexagonal ports/adapters; functional core and imperative shell; explicit constructor injection. PM pij-right-kotallo owns shared contracts and final production wiring; three coder lanes build independently against the committed baseline. Prefer existing Flowspace pure configuration/error/output/testing ideas, not its daemon/Postgres/ML dependencies. Standard-first telemetry and simple per-harness adapters remain later contracts, not premature foundation code.
architecture.composition_root: crates/app/src/main.rs: real SDK Inspector/StdConfigReader -> CLI run; SDK facade also composes the same reader for direct callers. No service depends on CLI/app.
contracts: Scope: Plan001 foundation only. The standard-first OTLP/GenAI decision governs later telemetry work; no native reader, normalized telemetry schema, pij enrichment implementation or scratch-code import ships in this plan. Configuration-command responses are not telemetry records.

Crate graph: unisphere-core has pure DTOs, enums and ports (serde only; no filesystem, process, environment, Tokio, network or database). unisphere-sdk -> core + serde_json; unisphere-cli (frontend library) -> core + clap + serde_json; unisphere-testkit -> core + serde_json + tempfile (dev/proof only). A final unisphere-app binary crate -> sdk + cli; bin name unisphere. Production sdk/cli/app must never depend on testkit. Services never import CLI/app or concrete adapters; the SDK composition facade may select its local filesystem adapter.

Cargo independence: root Cargo.toml uses resolver=3, members=["crates/*"], shared edition=2024/version=0.1.0 and workspace dependency declarations. Baseline creates only real core/testkit crates; each coder adds its complete crate with core/testkit dependencies and is tested without sibling implementations. Root Cargo.toml belongs to tk-0001. Cargo.lock is single-owner PM-generated state in tk-0004, not a frozen baseline file: the same PM is explicitly authorized to materialize/commit it during baseline prep and refresh it during lane verification/composition. Coders never deliver lockfile changes. No live nested Cargo.toml is stored under testkit fixtures; manifests are Cargo.toml.template/data materialized into isolated temporary roots.

Core types: Configuration { source_roots: Vec<String> } defaults to []; ConfigOverrides { source_roots: Option<Vec<String>> } defaults to None; ConfigSource = Defaults | Inline(Vec<u8>) | File(PathBuf); InspectionRequest { source: ConfigSource, overrides: ConfigOverrides }; InspectionReport { configuration: Configuration }. Derive Debug/Clone/PartialEq as appropriate and Serialize for report/configuration. Do not serialize ConfigSource/InspectionRequest into diagnostics because they contain input bytes.

Core failures: ReadFailure = NotFound | PermissionDenied | TooLarge | Other; FailureKind = InvalidConfiguration | ConfigurationRead | InvalidArguments; Location { path: Option<String>, field: Option<String>, line: Option<u32>, column: Option<u32> }. Failure has private fields and public constructors invalid_configuration(location:Option<Location>)->Self, configuration_read(kind:ReadFailure, location:Option<Location>)->Self and invalid_arguments(location:Option<Location>)->Self. Accessors: kind()->FailureKind, location()->Option<&Location>, read_failure()->Option<ReadFailure>, code()/message()/fix()->&str and retryable()->bool. It implements Error/Display. Code/message/fix copy is core-owned and fixed, never caller-controlled: UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, UNI-CONFIG-READ, UNI-ARGS-INVALID; retryable=false in this scope. Never forward raw parser/UTF8/clap Debug errors or input values into diagnostics; known field locations and supplied file paths may identify a failure without full config text.

Core ports: pub trait ConfigReader: Send + Sync { fn read(&self, path: &Path, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReadFailure>; } and pub trait InspectionApi: Send + Sync { fn inspect(&self, request: &InspectionRequest) -> Result<InspectionReport, Failure>; }. These are synchronous explicit calls, with no hidden tasks or global registry. MAX_CONFIG_BYTES = 1_048_576 applies to inline bytes and file reads; readers reject oversize before copying unbounded input. Oversized Inline bytes return Failure::invalid_configuration(None), UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, without invoking ConfigReader. Oversized File input is ReadFailure::TooLarge mapped to Failure::configuration_read(...), UNI-CONFIG-READ with file location. Neither path attempts an unbounded copy.

Configuration semantics: JSON object with optional source_roots array of strings; {} and {"source_roots":[]} are valid. Reject malformed/non-UTF8 JSON, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-array roots, non-string roots and strings whose trim() is empty. Preserve valid root strings, order and duplicates exactly: no trimming, tilde/env expansion, canonicalization, directory existence probing or session reads. Defaults < present document source_roots < Some(overrides.source_roots); Some([]) explicitly clears. Validate each supplied layer, including overridden invalid values, so bad configuration is not silently hidden. File source must be an explicit absolute path; a relative File path is InvalidConfiguration. Roots themselves may remain relative and uninterpreted.

SDK contract: pub struct Inspector<R: ConfigReader>; Inspector::new(reader:R) uses Configuration::default(); Inspector::with_defaults(reader:R, defaults:Configuration) retains caller defaults and validates them on inspect; impl InspectionApi for Inspector<R>. Public StdConfigReader implements ConfigReader with bounded explicit-file reads. pub fn inspect(request:&InspectionRequest)->Result<InspectionReport,Failure> composes Inspector::new(StdConfigReader), never reads ambient config. Re-export the core request/report/config/error types at the SDK facade, not a second DTO model. Parser/resolution functions take bytes or typed values and do not perform IO; the service owns precedence/error mapping, the concrete reader owns disk access.

CLI contract: unisphere config check [--config PATH] [--source-root ROOT ... | --clear-source-roots] [--json | --human], plus --help and --version. No config flag means Defaults; repeated --source-root replaces the document list, --clear-source-roots means Some([]), and the two forms conflict. Capture working directory and terminal status only in main, then pass CliContext { cwd: PathBuf, stdout_is_terminal: bool, version: String } explicitly. pub fn run(args: impl IntoIterator<Item=OsString>, context:&CliContext, inspector:&dyn InspectionApi, stdout:&mut dyn Write, stderr:&mut dyn Write)->u8. Args include argv[0]. Resolve only the explicitly supplied config path against context.cwd before calling the port. CLI frontend must not import unisphere-sdk.

CLI response contract: machine output is exactly one JSON object plus LF on stdout: {"ok":true,"command":"config.check","v":1,"data":{"configuration":{"source_roots":[...]}}} or {"ok":false,"command":"config.check","v":1,"error":{"kind":"invalid_configuration|configuration_read|invalid_arguments","code":"...","message":"...","fix":"...","retryable":false,"location":null|{...}}}; success omits error, failure omits data. --json wins error rendering if conflicting flags are supplied, otherwise explicit mode precedes terminal detection; captured/piped output defaults JSON. No environment-mode override is added in this scope. Human success goes stdout, human failure stderr; diagnostic logs never contaminate machine stdout. Help/version honor the selected mode with command help/version and data.text/data.version, exit0; they do not invoke InspectionApi. Operational/config failures exit1; argument errors exit2. Failed output writes exit1 with a safe terse stderr message when possible.

Baseline fake/fixture contract: FakeReader accepts a caller-supplied absolute-path map of byte/error results and records read calls; FakeInspector accepts a configured Result and records requests; neither accesses disk/env/network. Shared fixtures cover empty/default/document/override settings, malformed JSON, wrong type, blank roots, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-string roots, sensitive-marker invalid-UTF8 bytes, missing/permission errors and expected categories. An on-demand oversized_document() generates otherwise-valid JSON one byte over MAX_CONFIG_BYTES without embedding a megabyte file. All lanes consume the same negative fixtures for applicable SDK/CLI parity cases. Baseline tests prove these real fake/fixture contracts, not a future SDK/CLI. sealed_command(binary:&Path, temp_root:&Path)->std::io::Result<std::process::Command> requires an absolute executable, creates only caller-authorized temporary HOME/config roots and builds (does not run) a child with cleared environment and PATH="". It retains only explicitly required platform variables, never HOME/XDG_*/UNISPHERE_*/tokens from the parent. The proof tool uses a separate explicit build environment for cargo/rustc, then runs the built product through sealed_command with Node/OMP/Builder inaccessible. Hostile environment values are set on the child Command before spawn, never by mutating the proof process environment.

PM composition root: crates/app/src/main.rs captures explicit process context and passes a real unisphere_sdk::Inspector<StdConfigReader> into unisphere_cli::run, using explicit ExitCode handling rather than Result-main Debug dumps. App/Cargo.toml names bin unisphere and links sdk/cli; neither lane needs app to exist. External-consumer proof creates an isolated Cargo package with a path dependency on sdk and calls its public facade from outside the repository; installed-CLI proof uses cargo install --path crates/app --root <temporary-root> and executes the installed binary. No Node, Builder or daemon is required by the built SDK/CLI at runtime.

Proof boundary: planned commands below become executable when their owning unit is implemented; guide validation/review does not execute or claim them. Native reader scratch tests are separate and cannot satisfy Plan001 acceptance. Main/PM owns validation and formatting across unit deliveries; coders author code/tests but do not race global gates or formatters. Future changes to a frozen shared signature require explicit guide/baseline reconciliation before dependent release, not hand-edited packets.

Toolchain contract: Rust 1.95.0/edition 2024 is the selected compiler target. rust-toolchain.toml is a rustup request, not proof of enforcement. The earlier PATH-only probe missed an installed rustup toolchain; current actual evidence is assets/toolchain-observation.json. The approved coherent tuple is rustc 1.95.0 commit 59807616e1fa2540724bfbac14d7976d7e4a3860, cargo 1.95.0 commit f2d3ce0bd7f24a49f8f72d9000448f8838c4e850, clippy 0.1.95 commit 59807616e1 and rustfmt 1.9.0-stable commit 59807616e1. Homebrew and rustup distributions may satisfy the same tuple: compare releases and commit identities, not installation paths, distribution labels or exact whole version strings; record resolved binary provenance separately. Before claiming product quality/boot gates, tk-0005 records actual rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt versions/provenance and fails with a named prerequisite on missing/mixed identity. Select equivalent installed binaries per command without automatic global install/change. Baseline tests use matching compiler/Cargo. meta.title: Unisphere foundation: independent SDK, CLI and proof lanes

architecture.principles: Hexagonal ports/adapters; functional core and imperative shell; explicit constructor injection. PM pij-right-kotallo owns shared contracts and final production wiring; three coder lanes build independently against the committed baseline. Prefer existing Flowspace pure configuration/error/output/testing ideas, not its daemon/Postgres/ML dependencies. Standard-first telemetry and simple per-harness adapters remain later contracts, not premature foundation code.
architecture.composition_root: crates/app/src/main.rs: real SDK Inspector/StdConfigReader -> CLI run; SDK facade also composes the same reader for direct callers. No service depends on CLI/app.
contracts: Scope: Plan001 foundation only. The standard-first OTLP/GenAI decision governs later telemetry work; no native reader, normalized telemetry schema, pij enrichment implementation or scratch-code import ships in this plan. Configuration-command responses are not telemetry records.

Crate graph: unisphere-core has pure DTOs, enums and ports (serde only; no filesystem, process, environment, Tokio, network or database). unisphere-sdk -> core + serde_json; unisphere-cli (frontend library) -> core + clap + serde_json; unisphere-testkit -> core + serde_json + tempfile (dev/proof only). A final unisphere-app binary crate -> sdk + cli; bin name unisphere. Production sdk/cli/app must never depend on testkit. Services never import CLI/app or concrete adapters; the SDK composition facade may select its local filesystem adapter.

Cargo independence: root Cargo.toml uses resolver=3, members=["crates/*"], shared edition=2024/version=0.1.0 and workspace dependency declarations. Baseline creates only real core/testkit crates; each coder adds its complete crate with core/testkit dependencies and is tested without sibling implementations. Root Cargo.toml belongs to tk-0001. Cargo.lock is single-owner PM-generated state in tk-0004, not a frozen baseline file: the same PM is explicitly authorized to materialize/commit it during baseline prep and refresh it during lane verification/composition. Coders never deliver lockfile changes. No live nested Cargo.toml is stored under testkit fixtures; manifests are Cargo.toml.template/data materialized into isolated temporary roots.

Core types: Configuration { source_roots: Vec<String> } defaults to []; ConfigOverrides { source_roots: Option<Vec<String>> } defaults to None; ConfigSource = Defaults | Inline(Vec<u8>) | File(PathBuf); InspectionRequest { source: ConfigSource, overrides: ConfigOverrides }; InspectionReport { configuration: Configuration }. Derive Debug/Clone/PartialEq as appropriate and Serialize for report/configuration. Do not serialize ConfigSource/InspectionRequest into diagnostics because they contain input bytes.

Core failures: ReadFailure = NotFound | PermissionDenied | TooLarge | Other; FailureKind = InvalidConfiguration | ConfigurationRead | InvalidArguments; Location { path: Option<String>, field: Option<String>, line: Option<u32>, column: Option<u32> }. Failure has private fields and public constructors invalid_configuration(location:Option<Location>)->Self, configuration_read(kind:ReadFailure, location:Option<Location>)->Self and invalid_arguments(location:Option<Location>)->Self. Accessors: kind()->FailureKind, location()->Option<&Location>, read_failure()->Option<ReadFailure>, code()/message()/fix()->&str and retryable()->bool. It implements Error/Display. Code/message/fix copy is core-owned and fixed, never caller-controlled: UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, UNI-CONFIG-READ, UNI-ARGS-INVALID; retryable=false in this scope. Never forward raw parser/UTF8/clap Debug errors or input values into diagnostics; known field locations and supplied file paths may identify a failure without full config text.

Core ports: pub trait ConfigReader: Send + Sync { fn read(&self, path: &Path, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReadFailure>; } and pub trait InspectionApi: Send + Sync { fn inspect(&self, request: &InspectionRequest) -> Result<InspectionReport, Failure>; }. These are synchronous explicit calls, with no hidden tasks or global registry. MAX_CONFIG_BYTES = 1_048_576 applies to inline bytes and file reads; readers reject oversize before copying unbounded input. Oversized Inline bytes return Failure::invalid_configuration(None), UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, without invoking ConfigReader. Oversized File input is ReadFailure::TooLarge mapped to Failure::configuration_read(...), UNI-CONFIG-READ with file location. Neither path attempts an unbounded copy.

Configuration semantics: JSON object with optional source_roots array of strings; {} and {"source_roots":[]} are valid. Reject malformed/non-UTF8 JSON, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-array roots, non-string roots and strings whose trim() is empty. Preserve valid root strings, order and duplicates exactly: no trimming, tilde/env expansion, canonicalization, directory existence probing or session reads. Defaults < present document source_roots < Some(overrides.source_roots); Some([]) explicitly clears. Validate each supplied layer, including overridden invalid values, so bad configuration is not silently hidden. File source must be an explicit absolute path; a relative File path is InvalidConfiguration. Roots themselves may remain relative and uninterpreted.

SDK contract: pub struct Inspector<R: ConfigReader>; Inspector::new(reader:R) uses Configuration::default(); Inspector::with_defaults(reader:R, defaults:Configuration) retains caller defaults and validates them on inspect; impl InspectionApi for Inspector<R>. Public StdConfigReader implements ConfigReader with bounded explicit-file reads. pub fn inspect(request:&InspectionRequest)->Result<InspectionReport,Failure> composes Inspector::new(StdConfigReader), never reads ambient config. Re-export the core request/report/config/error types at the SDK facade, not a second DTO model. Parser/resolution functions take bytes or typed values and do not perform IO; the service owns precedence/error mapping, the concrete reader owns disk access.

CLI contract: unisphere config check [--config PATH] [--source-root ROOT ... | --clear-source-roots] [--json | --human], plus --help and --version. No config flag means Defaults; repeated --source-root replaces the document list, --clear-source-roots means Some([]), and the two forms conflict. Capture working directory and terminal status only in main, then pass CliContext { cwd: PathBuf, stdout_is_terminal: bool, version: String } explicitly. pub fn run(args: impl IntoIterator<Item=OsString>, context:&CliContext, inspector:&dyn InspectionApi, stdout:&mut dyn Write, stderr:&mut dyn Write)->u8. Args include argv[0]. Resolve only the explicitly supplied config path against context.cwd before calling the port. CLI frontend must not import unisphere-sdk.

CLI response contract: machine output is exactly one JSON object plus LF on stdout: {"ok":true,"command":"config.check","v":1,"data":{"configuration":{"source_roots":[...]}}} or {"ok":false,"command":"config.check","v":1,"error":{"kind":"invalid_configuration|configuration_read|invalid_arguments","code":"...","message":"...","fix":"...","retryable":false,"location":null|{...}}}; success omits error, failure omits data. --json wins error rendering if conflicting flags are supplied, otherwise explicit mode precedes terminal detection; captured/piped output defaults JSON. No environment-mode override is added in this scope. Human success goes stdout, human failure stderr; diagnostic logs never contaminate machine stdout. Help/version honor the selected mode with command help/version and data.text/data.version, exit0; they do not invoke InspectionApi. Operational/config failures exit1; argument errors exit2. Failed output writes exit1 with a safe terse stderr message when possible.

Baseline fake/fixture contract: FakeReader accepts a caller-supplied absolute-path map of byte/error results and records read calls; FakeInspector accepts a configured Result and records requests; neither accesses disk/env/network. Shared fixtures cover empty/default/document/override settings, malformed JSON, wrong type, blank roots, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-string roots, sensitive-marker invalid-UTF8 bytes, missing/permission errors and expected categories. An on-demand oversized_document() generates otherwise-valid JSON one byte over MAX_CONFIG_BYTES without embedding a megabyte file. All lanes consume the same negative fixtures for applicable SDK/CLI parity cases. Baseline tests prove these real fake/fixture contracts, not a future SDK/CLI. sealed_command(binary:&Path, temp_root:&Path)->std::io::Result<std::process::Command> requires an absolute executable, creates only caller-authorized temporary HOME/config roots and builds (does not run) a child with cleared environment and PATH="". It retains only explicitly required platform variables, never HOME/XDG_*/UNISPHERE_*/tokens from the parent. The proof tool uses a separate explicit build environment for cargo/rustc, then runs the built product through sealed_command with Node/OMP/Builder inaccessible. Hostile environment values are set on the child Command before spawn, never by mutating the proof process environment.

PM composition root: crates/app/src/main.rs captures explicit process context and passes a real unisphere_sdk::Inspector<StdConfigReader> into unisphere_cli::run, using explicit ExitCode handling rather than Result-main Debug dumps. App/Cargo.toml names bin unisphere and links sdk/cli; neither lane needs app to exist. External-consumer proof creates an isolated Cargo package with a path dependency on sdk and calls its public facade from outside the repository; installed-CLI proof uses cargo install --path crates/app --root <temporary-root> and executes the installed binary. No Node, Builder or daemon is required by the built SDK/CLI at runtime.

Proof boundary: planned commands below become executable when their owning unit is implemented; guide validation/review does not execute or claim them. Native reader scratch tests are separate and cannot satisfy Plan001 acceptance. Main/PM owns validation and formatting across unit deliveries; coders author code/tests but do not race global gates or formatters. Future changes to a frozen shared signature require explicit guide/baseline reconciliation before dependent release, not hand-edited packets.

Toolchain contract: Rust 1.95.0/edition 2024 is the selected compiler target. rust-toolchain.toml is a rustup request, not proof of enforcement. The earlier PATH-only probe missed an installed rustup toolchain; current actual evidence is assets/toolchain-observation.json. The approved coherent tuple is rustc 1.95.0 commit 59807616e1fa2540724bfbac14d7976d7e4a3860, cargo 1.95.0 commit f2d3ce0bd7f24a49f8f72d9000448f8838c4e850, clippy 0.1.95 commit 59807616e1 and rustfmt 1.9.0-stable commit 59807616e1. Homebrew and rustup distributions may satisfy the same tuple: compare releases and commit identities, not installation paths, distribution labels or exact whole version strings; record resolved binary provenance separately. Before claiming product quality/boot gates, tk-0005 records actual rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt versions/provenance and fails with a named prerequisite on missing/mixed identity. Select equivalent installed binaries per command without automatic global install/change. Baseline tests use matching compiler/Cargo. Product crates exclude Node/native-ML/database dependencies; additional platform support requires observed CI evidence.

Proof-grade boundary: source/dependency review must explicitly confirm that core and SDK contain no ambient configuration reads, network/client calls, process launches, FFI or unsafe-code escape, beyond the permitted ConfigReader call. Core/SDK forbid unsafe code and the dependency allowlist excludes networking/runtime crates, but dependency absence alone is not a syscall trace. The sealed external consumer provides automated evidence of no observed ambient influence; the no-network promise additionally requires named independent source-surface review. Do not describe that judgement as an executed network-denial test or weaken ac-0008.

fan_out.rationale: Operator-approved PM pij-right-kotallo plus three reusable coder lanes: SDK/config service, CLI frontend, and proof/tooling. All consume the same core ports/fakes/fixtures and can compile/test without a finished sibling. PM commits/seals the small baseline first, releases all three ready units together, imports completed deliveries through Builder, and composes after their contracts are satisfied. Add/reuse coders only for another genuinely independent ready unit; no artificial SDK-then-CLI barrier.

meta.title: Unisphere foundation: independent SDK, CLI and proof lanes

architecture.principles: Hexagonal ports/adapters; functional core and imperative shell; explicit constructor injection. PM pij-right-kotallo owns shared contracts and final production wiring; three coder lanes build independently against the committed baseline. Prefer existing Flowspace pure configuration/error/output/testing ideas, not its daemon/Postgres/ML dependencies. Standard-first telemetry and simple per-harness adapters remain later contracts, not premature foundation code.
architecture.composition_root: crates/app/src/main.rs: real SDK Inspector/StdConfigReader -> CLI run; SDK facade also composes the same reader for direct callers. No service depends on CLI/app.
contracts: Scope: Plan001 foundation only. The standard-first OTLP/GenAI decision governs later telemetry work; no native reader, normalized telemetry schema, pij enrichment implementation or scratch-code import ships in this plan. Configuration-command responses are not telemetry records.

Crate graph: unisphere-core has pure DTOs, enums and ports (serde only; no filesystem, process, environment, Tokio, network or database). unisphere-sdk -> core + serde_json; unisphere-cli (frontend library) -> core + clap + serde_json; unisphere-testkit -> core + serde_json + tempfile (dev/proof only). A final unisphere-app binary crate -> sdk + cli; bin name unisphere. Production sdk/cli/app must never depend on testkit. Services never import CLI/app or concrete adapters; the SDK composition facade may select its local filesystem adapter.

Cargo independence: root Cargo.toml uses resolver=3, members=["crates/*"], shared edition=2024/version=0.1.0 and workspace dependency declarations. Baseline creates only real core/testkit crates; each coder adds its complete crate with core/testkit dependencies and is tested without sibling implementations. Root Cargo.toml belongs to tk-0001. Cargo.lock is single-owner PM-generated state in tk-0004, not a frozen baseline file: the same PM is explicitly authorized to materialize/commit it during baseline prep and refresh it during lane verification/composition. Coders never deliver lockfile changes. No live nested Cargo.toml is stored under testkit fixtures; manifests are Cargo.toml.template/data materialized into isolated temporary roots.

Core types: Configuration { source_roots: Vec<String> } defaults to []; ConfigOverrides { source_roots: Option<Vec<String>> } defaults to None; ConfigSource = Defaults | Inline(Vec<u8>) | File(PathBuf); InspectionRequest { source: ConfigSource, overrides: ConfigOverrides }; InspectionReport { configuration: Configuration }. Derive Debug/Clone/PartialEq as appropriate and Serialize for report/configuration. Do not serialize ConfigSource/InspectionRequest into diagnostics because they contain input bytes.

Core failures: ReadFailure = NotFound | PermissionDenied | TooLarge | Other; FailureKind = InvalidConfiguration | ConfigurationRead | InvalidArguments; Location { path: Option<String>, field: Option<String>, line: Option<u32>, column: Option<u32> }. Failure has private fields and public constructors invalid_configuration(location:Option<Location>)->Self, configuration_read(kind:ReadFailure, location:Option<Location>)->Self and invalid_arguments(location:Option<Location>)->Self. Accessors: kind()->FailureKind, location()->Option<&Location>, read_failure()->Option<ReadFailure>, code()/message()/fix()->&str and retryable()->bool. It implements Error/Display. Code/message/fix copy is core-owned and fixed, never caller-controlled: UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, UNI-CONFIG-READ, UNI-ARGS-INVALID; retryable=false in this scope. Never forward raw parser/UTF8/clap Debug errors or input values into diagnostics; known field locations and supplied file paths may identify a failure without full config text.

Core ports: pub trait ConfigReader: Send + Sync { fn read(&self, path: &Path, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReadFailure>; } and pub trait InspectionApi: Send + Sync { fn inspect(&self, request: &InspectionRequest) -> Result<InspectionReport, Failure>; }. These are synchronous explicit calls, with no hidden tasks or global registry. MAX_CONFIG_BYTES = 1_048_576 applies to inline bytes and file reads; readers reject oversize before copying unbounded input. Oversized Inline bytes return Failure::invalid_configuration(None), UNI-CONFIG-INVALID, without invoking ConfigReader. Oversized File input is ReadFailure::TooLarge mapped to Failure::configuration_read(...), UNI-CONFIG-READ with file location. Neither path attempts an unbounded copy.

Configuration semantics: JSON object with optional source_roots array of strings; {} and {"source_roots":[]} are valid. Reject malformed/non-UTF8 JSON, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-array roots, non-string roots and strings whose trim() is empty. Preserve valid root strings, order and duplicates exactly: no trimming, tilde/env expansion, canonicalization, directory existence probing or session reads. Defaults < present document source_roots < Some(overrides.source_roots); Some([]) explicitly clears. Validate each supplied layer, including overridden invalid values, so bad configuration is not silently hidden. File source must be an explicit absolute path; a relative File path is InvalidConfiguration. Roots themselves may remain relative and uninterpreted.

SDK contract: pub struct Inspector<R: ConfigReader>; Inspector::new(reader:R) uses Configuration::default(); Inspector::with_defaults(reader:R, defaults:Configuration) retains caller defaults and validates them on inspect; impl InspectionApi for Inspector<R>. Public StdConfigReader implements ConfigReader with bounded explicit-file reads. pub fn inspect(request:&InspectionRequest)->Result<InspectionReport,Failure> composes Inspector::new(StdConfigReader), never reads ambient config. Re-export the core request/report/config/error types at the SDK facade, not a second DTO model. Parser/resolution functions take bytes or typed values and do not perform IO; the service owns precedence/error mapping, the concrete reader owns disk access.

CLI contract: unisphere config check [--config PATH] [--source-root ROOT ... | --clear-source-roots] [--json | --human], plus --help and --version. No config flag means Defaults; repeated --source-root replaces the document list, --clear-source-roots means Some([]), and the two forms conflict. Capture working directory and terminal status only in main, then pass CliContext { cwd: PathBuf, stdout_is_terminal: bool, version: String } explicitly. pub fn run(args: impl IntoIterator<Item=OsString>, context:&CliContext, inspector:&dyn InspectionApi, stdout:&mut dyn Write, stderr:&mut dyn Write)->u8. Args include argv[0]. Resolve only the explicitly supplied config path against context.cwd before calling the port. CLI frontend must not import unisphere-sdk.

CLI response contract: machine output is exactly one JSON object plus LF on stdout: {"ok":true,"command":"config.check","v":1,"data":{"configuration":{"source_roots":[...]}}} or {"ok":false,"command":"config.check","v":1,"error":{"kind":"invalid_configuration|configuration_read|invalid_arguments","code":"...","message":"...","fix":"...","retryable":false,"location":null|{...}}}; success omits error, failure omits data. --json wins error rendering if conflicting flags are supplied, otherwise explicit mode precedes terminal detection; captured/piped output defaults JSON. No environment-mode override is added in this scope. Human success goes stdout, human failure stderr; diagnostic logs never contaminate machine stdout. Help/version honor the selected mode with command help/version and data.text/data.version, exit0; they do not invoke InspectionApi. Operational/config failures exit1; argument errors exit2. Failed output writes exit1 with a safe terse stderr message when possible.

Baseline fake/fixture contract: FakeReader accepts a caller-supplied absolute-path map of byte/error results and records read calls; FakeInspector accepts a configured Result and records requests; neither accesses disk/env/network. Shared fixtures cover empty/default/document/override settings, malformed JSON, wrong type, blank roots, non-object documents, unknown keys, duplicate known keys, non-string roots, sensitive-marker invalid-UTF8 bytes, missing/permission errors and expected categories. An on-demand oversized_document() generates otherwise-valid JSON one byte over MAX_CONFIG_BYTES without embedding a megabyte file. All lanes consume the same negative fixtures for applicable SDK/CLI parity cases. Baseline tests prove these real fake/fixture contracts, not a future SDK/CLI. sealed_command(binary:&Path, temp_root:&Path)->std::io::Result<std::process::Command> requires an absolute executable, creates only caller-authorized temporary HOME/config roots and builds (does not run) a child with cleared environment and PATH="". It retains only explicitly required platform variables, never HOME/XDG_*/UNISPHERE_*/tokens from the parent. The proof tool uses a separate explicit build environment for cargo/rustc, then runs the built product through sealed_command with Node/OMP/Builder inaccessible. Hostile environment values are set on the child Command before spawn, never by mutating the proof process environment.

PM composition root: crates/app/src/main.rs captures explicit process context and passes a real unisphere_sdk::Inspector<StdConfigReader> into unisphere_cli::run, using explicit ExitCode handling rather than Result-main Debug dumps. App/Cargo.toml names bin unisphere and links sdk/cli; neither lane needs app to exist. External-consumer proof creates an isolated Cargo package with a path dependency on sdk and calls its public facade from outside the repository; installed-CLI proof uses cargo install --path crates/app --root <temporary-root> and executes the installed binary. No Node, Builder or daemon is required by the built SDK/CLI at runtime.

Proof boundary: planned commands below become executable when their owning unit is implemented; guide validation/review does not execute or claim them. Native reader scratch tests are separate and cannot satisfy Plan001 acceptance. Main/PM owns validation and formatting across unit deliveries; coders author code/tests but do not race global gates or formatters. Future changes to a frozen shared signature require explicit guide/baseline reconciliation before dependent release, not hand-edited packets.

Toolchain contract: Rust 1.95.0/edition 2024 is the selected compiler target. rust-toolchain.toml is a rustup request, not proof of enforcement. The earlier PATH-only probe missed an installed rustup toolchain; current actual evidence is assets/toolchain-observation.json. The approved coherent tuple is rustc 1.95.0 commit 59807616e1fa2540724bfbac14d7976d7e4a3860, cargo 1.95.0 commit f2d3ce0bd7f24a49f8f72d9000448f8838c4e850, clippy 0.1.95 commit 59807616e1 and rustfmt 1.9.0-stable commit 59807616e1. Homebrew and rustup distributions may satisfy the same tuple: compare releases and commit identities, not installation paths, distribution labels or exact whole version strings; record resolved binary provenance separately. Before claiming product quality/boot gates, tk-0005 records actual rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt versions/provenance and fails with a named prerequisite on missing/mixed identity. Select equivalent installed binaries per command without automatic global install/change. Baseline tests use matching compiler/Cargo. Product crates exclude Node/native-ML/database dependencies; additional platform support requires observed CI evidence.

Proof-grade boundary: source/dependency review must explicitly confirm that core and SDK contain no ambient configuration reads, network/client calls, process launches, FFI or unsafe-code escape, beyond the permitted ConfigReader call. Core/SDK forbid unsafe code and the dependency allowlist excludes networking/runtime crates, but dependency absence alone is not a syscall trace. The sealed external consumer provides automated evidence of no observed ambient influence; the no-network promise additionally requires named independent source-surface review. Do not describe that judgement as an executed network-denial test or weaken ac-0008.

PM commits/seals the small baseline first, releases all three ready units together, imports completed deliveries through Builder, and composes after their contracts are satisfied. Add/reuse coders only for another genuinely independent ready unit; no artificial SDK-then-CLI barrier.
